sanskrit:
शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात्।
कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः।।
image_english: One who tolerates the urges of desire and anger before leaving the body is a yogī and is happy.
caption:
Chapter 5, Verse 23

Kṛṣṇa challenges Arjuna to control the forces of impulse. ‘śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṁ’ (Before giving up this present body, if one is able to tolerate). ‘prāk śarīra-vimokṣaṇāt’. ‘kāma-krodhodbhavaṁ vegaṁ’ (The urges of material desire and anger). ‘sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ’ (He is a yogī and is happy in this world). The urges come like waves (‘vegam’). You cannot stop the wave, but you can learn to surf it without drowning. If you can hold your tongue when angry and hold your mind when lusty, you have passed the test of human life.
